title: Audit Provenance Gatekeeper - tooling spec and runbook (draft)
body:
Purpose:
This doc describes a lightweight "Gatekeeper" service to sit in front of evidence collectors and SIEM exporters. The Gatekeeper enforces provenance checks, TTL rules, RBAC v2 scoping, and decides whether to forward, redact, or enrich events for long-term evidence storage. The goal is to reduce manual triage, improve signal quality for SIEM consumers, and centralize policy enforcement for control evidence.

Scope and non-goals:
- In-scope: collector-side integration patterns, Gatekeeper decision contract, audit schema mapping for SIEM export, operator runbook, failure modes, simple rollout strategy.
- Not in-scope: full SIEM schema transformation service, data lake retention implementation, end-user UI.

Design principles:
- Minimal latency impact for high-throughput collectors (target added p99 latency < 15ms per event).
- Deterministic decisions: given same event + policy state, Gatekeeper outputs same action.
- Policy-first: policies expressed as JSON + versioned. Policies can include RBAC-derived allow/deny lists, TTL overrides, and provenance score thresholds.
- Fail-open configurable by route: critical control evidence should default to fail-closed; noisy telemetry can fail-open.

High-level architecture:
- Collector -> Gatekeeper (sidecar or central) -> Evidence Router -> Archive/SIEM exporter
- Gatekeeper has three functional modules: Ingest/normalizer, Policy engine, Enrichment/transformer.
- Gatekeeper stores short-lived checkpoints (stream offsets, last-hash) in a compact KeyValue store for replay transparency.

Event contract (simplified audit event):
Each event the Gatekeeper accepts MUST be valid JSON with at least these fields:
- event_id: string (uuid)
- timestamp: ISO-8601 string
- source: string (service name, e.g., "dedicated-controller")
- actor: object stringified or token (see RBAC integration below)
- action: string (create, update, invoke, authz_check, etc.)
- resource: string (resource path or identifier)
- proto_schema: string (optional, used for structured payloads)
- payload: base64 or json (opaque to Gatekeeper; can be parsed by enrichment)
- evidence_level: one of [control, infra, telemetry] (defaults to telemetry)
- provenance: object string (see sample below)

Sample provenance payload (stored as JSON string in provenance field):
{
  "origin": "k8s-audit", 
  "collector_id": "harvester-11",
  "hash_chain": "b1946ac92492d2347c6235b4d2611184",
  "received_at": "2026-02-11T18:22:34Z",
  "verifier": "gatekeeper-v0.3",
  "score": 0.86
}

Policy engine (contract):
Policies are versioned JSON with the following keys:
- id (string)
- scope (list of paths or wildcarded sources)
- allow_if (list of boolean expressions over event fields, RBAC attributes, provenance.score)
- redact_fields (list of jsonpaths)
- ttl_seconds (integer)
- fallback_action: one of [forward, redact, drop, quarantine]
- revised_by (string, optional)
- enforced (boolean)
Example policy: "control-ttl-v1" enforces that evidence_level==control and ttl_seconds>=31536000 (1y) and fallback_action==quarantine for noncompliant items.

RBAC v2 integration notes:
- Gatekeeper does not duplicate RBAC evaluation: it calls the RBAC v2 service (HTTP gRPC) to fetch a compact token (rbac_context) for the actor. This context includes: roles, org_id, resource-scoped grants and implicit grants.
- Policy expressions can reference rbac_context fields (e.g., rbac_context.roles contains "auditor").
- For performance, Gatekeeper caches rbac_context entries for short TTLs (configurable, default 60s) and stamps decisions with the rbac_fetch_version.
- Edge case: when RBAC service is unavailable, route-level fallback determines behaviour (fail-open for telemetry; fail-closed for control).

SIEM export mapping:
We keep a compact canonical mapping and a per-siem adapter:
Canonical fields -> SIEM field (example Splunk)
- event_id -> event_id
- timestamp -> _time
- source -> source\\_service
- actor.identity -> actor
- action -> action
- resource -> object\\_name
- evidence_level -> classification
- provenance.score -> provenance_score (float)
- provenance.hash_chain -> evidence_chain
- gatekeeper_decision -> decision
- gatekeeper_policy_id -> policy_id
Note: redaction is applied prior to mapping. Redacted fields are replaced with the token "[REDACTED]" and a redaction_mask list is appended to the event._meta.redactions for audit.

Collector plugin API (recommended minimal surface):
- /v1/ingest (POST) -> accepts a batch of events (ndjson or json array). Returns per-event status with acknowledgements and optional sequence token for checkpointing.
- /v1/health -> liveness and last-policy-version
- /v1/metrics -> prometheus endpoint for counters (ingested, forwarded, dropped, latency_histogram)
- /v1/checkpoint (POST) -> accept sequence token for durable checkpointing (optional)
- TLS mTLS required; client cert indicates collector identity.

Operational runbook (oncall-friendly):
1) Symptom: Gatekeeper returning large number of "quarantine" decisions
   - Check policy version: gatekeeper/admin -> policies (was a strict policy rolled last deploy?)
   - Review recent rb_running_changes or RBAC service errors in logs.
   - If emergency, set fallback_action for affected route to "forward" and open an incident.
2) Symptom: p99 ingestion latency spikes
   - Check enrichers: any heavy parsing (proto decode) enabled? Disable optional enrichers per route.
   - Check kv-store latency (checkpointing) and fallback to async checkpointing.
3) Symptom: SIEM shows many [REDACTED] fields unexpectedly
   - Trace policy_id in event._meta.policy_id back to policy content; verify redaction jsonpaths.

Failure modes and mitigation ideas:
- Gatekeeper crash loop: use sidecar restart budget and circuit-breaker in router to direct to backup gatekeeper.
- RBAC timeout: implement cached decisions and clear cache on RBAC service recovery; add metrics for rbac_cache_hit_ratio.
- Checkpoint store unavailability: allow collector to switch to direct batch-forward to SIEM with a special header "x-forward-bypassed-gatekeeper: true" (audit-only and rate-limited).

Data retention and TTL enforcement:
- Gatekeeper enforces or annotates TTL on forwarded events (ttl_seconds field). Long-term archive should honor the TTL.
- When a policy shortens TTL (e.g., redaction), Gatekeeper writes policy_id and policy_digest into event._meta for future audits.

Rollout plan (canary -> global):
- Stage 0: deploy Gatekeeper as read-only analyzer (no decisions, only metrics + policy violations report) for 3 days.
- Stage 1: enable decisions on telemetry routes (fail-open) with 10% sampled control forwarding.
- Stage 2: expand to 50% traffic for telemetry, add quarantining for noncompliant controls in a holding queue.
- Stage 3: enforce globally with full TTL and quarantine semantics.

Acceptance criteria for GA:
- p99 additional latency per event < 15ms for 90% of routes
- policy evaluation correctness verified for 2000 randomized test events
- RBAC service cache hit ratio >= 0.8 in steady state
- SIEM adapter round-trip mapping verified for Splunk and Elastic adapters

Outstanding work / open questions (todo):
- Formalize policy language (subset of CEL or Rego?). We need tradeoffs: CEL is lower overhead; Rego is more expressive.
- Decide canonical hash function for hash_chain and format of chain entries (HMAC vs raw sha256).
- Backfill strategy for existing archived evidence missing provenance fields.
- Demo script for oncall to unquarantine items and resubmit to archive.

Notes to reviewers:
- This is intentionally pragmatic; we prioritize a small policy surface and predictable behaviour over trying to handle all cases.
- Please annotate the policy examples you think are too strict or too lax.

Historical context links and references:
- See linked_artifacts for the POC PR.
- Related: provenance-envelope-collector-adapter-spec (audit interoperability)

-- end --
